title: Charges loom for 114 erring gas stations
summary: The Department of Energy is preparing to take legal action against 114 gas stations that failed to comply with last week’s major fuel price rollback.

blocks.text: Motorists queue at a gasoline station in Marikina on July 27, 2026.
MANILA, Philippines — The Department of Energy (DOE) is preparing to take legal action against 114 gas stations that failed to comply with last week’s major fuel price rollback.
The DOE’s field offices inspected 213 gas stations from Nov. 10 to 13, the week the agency ordered players to cut gasoline prices by a whopping P16.80 per liter.

“Unfortunately, 114 were found not to have implemented exactly what was mandated,” DOE-Oil Industry Management Bureau director Rino Abad said at a virtual press conference yesterday. “Instead of P16, they cut prices at only P10 or P12.”
The DOE did not specify where the non-compliant gas stations were located.
With the Philippines still under a national energy emergency, the DOE has the authority to dictate price adjustments under the Downstream Oil Industry Deregulation Law.
Abad also cited Presidential Decree 1865, signed in 1983, which involves petroleum products and national security.
Those found guilty of violating the decree may be imprisoned for two to five years and fined between P20,000 and P50,000.
“Based on the discussions with our legal department, these two laws can be used for their assessment and appreciation in case these inspections turn into actual cases,” Abad said.
